integrated_multimodal_description

Create an 8-second full-body K-pop performance with a power-oriented groove and sleek hip-hop influence. Preserve the reference identity, facial structure, short layered hair under the gray cap, makeup, body proportions, red-and-black oversized varsity jacket, black crop top, layered necklaces, fingerless gloves, extremely baggy cream pants with straps and printed details, brown sneakers, gray studio background, soft frontal lighting, muted color grade, and original composition exactly. Add no props, accessories, costume changes, or background elements. At 0.00 seconds, use the source image itself as the exact first frame. Begin naturally from its wide stance, straight arms, forward gaze, and current weight distribution; no pose reset or position jump. Maintain realistic anatomy, stable facial identity, grounded foot contact, clear weight transfer, controlled full-body amplitude, and physically delayed hair, jacket, loose trouser, and strap motion. The character performs with cool, restrained confidence and precise camera-facing expression.

[00:00-00:01.10]
From the exact anchored pose, initiate through the feet: press the left foot into the floor, soften both knees, and shift the pelvis slightly left while the right heel pivots inward. Let that lower-body torque travel upward into a compact rightward rib isolation and shoulder recoil. The right elbow then sweeps diagonally across the torso at chest level while the left forearm opens low and outward, creating an asymmetric silhouette. Keep the chin nearly level and the eyes locked on the camera. The jacket sleeves and trouser fabric respond a fraction late, then begin to settle. Static full-body camera.

[00:01.10-00:02.25]
Use the shoulder recoil to launch a rightward cross-step: the left foot crosses behind the right, then the right foot steps wide to catch the weight in a lowered stance. The hips redirect right as the torso spirals three-quarter left against them. Both elbows carve a compact circular wrap around the ribs, then the right forearm releases forward in a crisp diagonal strike while the left arm remains bent near the waist. The head follows last, snapping from three-quarter left back toward the lens. The loose pant legs compress and swing around the knees; hanging straps trail behind the direction change. Camera trucks subtly right to preserve centering.

[00:02.25-00:03.35]
Rebound out of the wide landing into a syncopated heel-toe sequence: rotate the right heel outward as the left toe pivots inward, reverse once, then lift the left knee to mid-height while balancing over the right leg. At the knee lift, contract the abdomen and make a sharp chest accent backward. The right arm scoops from low left to high right, led by the elbow, while the left hand traces a shorter path across the lower torso without framing the face. The lifted foot lands diagonally forward-left, becoming the support for the next phrase. The cap and short hair react minimally; jacket hem and trouser straps swing with delayed inertia. Add a restrained push-in timed to the knee-lift accent.

[00:03.35-00:04.55]
Signature movement: from the diagonal left landing, perform a “lock-and-slice” traveling motif. Sink into the left knee, slide the right foot laterally along the floor, and shift the ribs sharply opposite the traveling direction. The left elbow locks horizontally as the right forearm slices underneath it; immediately release the lock through a torso spiral, switch weight onto the sliding right foot, and unfold both arms into one strong broken diagonal—left arm low-forward, right arm high-back. Face three-quarter right, then cut the eyes directly to camera without changing the body angle. This is a freeze-and-release accent, not a static pose. Camera makes a gentle arc left around the dancer, ending near a three-quarter frontal view.

[00:04.55-00:05.55]
Release the diagonal through the right shoulder, allowing it to pull the torso into a low backward weight-rock. Step the left foot behind, bend both knees, and hinge the torso slightly forward with a grounded groove; then drive through the left foot to return forward. During the rock, the arms fold close to the ribs; on the forward drive, the left elbow leads a broad horizontal sweep while the right arm opens behind the body. The head remains delayed, looking briefly toward the left hand’s path before returning to the lens. The jacket opens and rebounds naturally over the torso; fabric movement follows the acceleration and deceleration. Camera eases back slightly to retain the full expanded arm line.

[00:05.55-00:06.65]
Carry the horizontal sweep into a two-step diagonal advance toward camera-right: right foot steps, left foot gathers without closing completely, then the right foot plants in a small lunge. Each step has a clean knee pulse and alternating hip redirection. Layer a chest-forward accent on the first step and a rib shift left on the second. The right arm retracts from the sweep into a bent guard near the shoulder while the left arm drives low-to-high across the body, ending in a crisp outward elbow line. Keep the expression cool and focused, with a slight chin dip on the final lunge. Camera tracks diagonally with the dancer and applies a subtle push-in, never cropping the shoes.

[00:06.65-00:07.35]
Push out of the lunge into a quick kick-ball-change: make a controlled low left-foot kick forward, place the left ball behind, then transfer decisively onto the right foot. The transfer sends a sharp contraction-release through the abdomen and chest. Both arms cross briefly at forearm level in front of the torso, then break apart asymmetrically—right hand extending low-forward and left elbow opening high-left. Turn from diagonal to front through a grounded pivot of the supporting right foot, without spinning. The trouser legs flare on the kick and reverse with visible delayed drag. Camera finishes its tracking movement and stabilizes frontally.

[00:07.35-00:08.00]
Resolve directly from the broken arm geometry: settle the left foot wide to recover a powerful base, straighten the right knee while keeping the left knee softly bent, and shift the pelvis left under a controlled torso counter-angle. The left arm descends from high-left into a firm bent line near the ribs as the right arm lengthens diagonally downward beside the thigh. Finish with shoulders squared almost front, chest lifted, chin slightly lowered, and direct eye contact. Hold only after the weight fully arrives, allowing the jacket sleeves, pant fabric, straps, and short hair to complete a brief natural settling motion. Use a very slight final push-in; no cut, sudden zoom, jump, or arbitrary freeze.

overall_soundscape

Subtle studio-room ambience, realistic sneaker contacts and soft sole squeaks, restrained fabric swishes from the oversized jacket and baggy trousers, faint strap movement, and light breathing synchronized with exertion. Keep movement sounds polished and understated, with no crowd noise or added props.
